briefings.title: Building Codex with Tibo Sottiaux

people.name: Tibo Sottiaux
people.role: Head of Core Products & Platform, OpenAI

briefings.tldr: Tibo Sottiaux, Head of Core Products & Platform at OpenAI, discusses the engineering behind Codex, its open-source and multi-provider architecture, and how AI is fundamentally transforming the software development lifecycle, code reviews, and maintenance within OpenAI.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Tibo Sottiaux, Head of Core Products & Platform at OpenAI, discusses the engineering behind Codex, its open-source and multi-provider architecture, and how AI is fundamentally transforming the software development lifecycle, code reviews, and maintenance within OpenAI.

## Codex Architecture: Rust, Open Source, and Model Optionality
* **Language Choice (Rust):** Codex was built in Rust from first principles to ensure a robust, secure, and scalable agent core. Tibo Sottiaux notes that while internal models weren't initially optimized for Rust, the static verification at compile time proved invaluable for agents.
* **Open Source Strategy:** The Codex CLI, SDK, and app server were released as open source to co-design with the community, lower onboarding friction for new hires, and stay aligned with the evolving role of code.
    * **Downsides:** Tibo highlights the tax of handling an "tsunami of random stuff" (low-quality contributions) and the sting of competitors copying features built in the open before release.
* **Model Agnosticism:** Codex is intentionally not tied exclusively to OpenAI models; users can plug in models from other providers. Tibo explains this offers users necessary optionality and prevents lock-in.

## Execution Environments and the Harness-Model Dynamic
* **Sandboxing & Local vs. Cloud Execution:** By default, Codex runs locally inside a secure sandbox. However, the system is shifting toward managed cloud VMs (Kata containers) to leverage more compute and free developers from keeping laptops open.
* **The Harness as a Crutch:** Tibo explains that the harness is always slightly ahead of the model, providing "crutches" (such as developer instructions and guardrails) to ensure reliability. 
    * As newer models improve, the developer message and the harness code shrink because the model inherently understands what the user wants.

## AI in the Software Development Lifecycle
* **Automated Code Review & Security:** OpenAI utilizes specialized review models trained to spot deep logic and security vulnerabilities across multiple dependency layers. Security issues automatically block pull requests from merging.
* **Zero-Cost Maintenance:** Maintenance is shifting from a tedious human tax to automated processes—such as automatically upgrading third-party dependencies and generating full rearchitectures in hours instead of years.
* **The "Merge" of Codex and ChatGPT:** Bringing Codex into ChatGPT required bridging two entirely different stacks: a fully managed cloud-based system and a local coding agent. The resulting setup runs the full Codex harness inside a powerful cloud container accessible via ChatGPT Plus.
* **Internal AI Logging:** Tibo shares that Codex acted as an internal "journalist," documenting Slack debates, document reviews, and the architectural naming decisions ("toggle arc") surrounding the ChatGPT/Codex merge.

## Notable Quotes
> *"If you're doing something and you know you're building like this 10,000 lines of code crutch to work around the model flaws, like you know, you're probably doing the wrong thing."*
> — **Tibo Sottiaux**

> *"The role of code review now is like... I think it was always about correctness... but it was also sort of like a little ritual for information exchange and bringing people on the same page. [...] I think that will be automated."*
> — **Tibo Sottiaux**

briefings.title: Can AI help us better predict the weather?

people.name: Peter Battaglia
people.role: Senior Director of Research, Google DeepMind

briefings.tldr: AI models developed by Google DeepMind—such as GraphCast, GenCast, and WeatherNext 3—are revolutionizing global weather forecasting by bypassing traditional supercomputer fluid dynamics approximations in favor of learning statistical patterns directly from decades of historical meteorological data, achieving significant performance gains including early warnings for extreme events like Category 5 storms.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
AI models developed by Google DeepMind—such as GraphCast, GenCast, and WeatherNext 3—are revolutionizing global weather forecasting by bypassing traditional supercomputer fluid dynamics approximations in favor of learning statistical patterns directly from decades of historical meteorological data, achieving significant performance gains including early warnings for extreme events like Category 5 storms.

## Podcast Background & Speakers
- **Host:** Professor Hannah Fry
- **Guest:** Peter Battaglia, Senior Director of Research at Google DeepMind
- **Setting & Context:** An episode of the *Google DeepMind Podcast* exploring how artificial intelligence is transforming global weather forecasting, predicting renewable energy supply and agricultural impacts, and reshaping numerical physics models.

## Real-World Impact: Hurricane Melissa Case Study
- **Early Warning Success:** In October 2025, Hurricane Melissa struck Jamaica and the Caribbean. Google DeepMind's weather lab website and live forecasts (developed via partnerships with agencies like NOAA's National Hurricane Center) began showing high confidence that the disturbance would become a Category 5 hurricane about a week before landfall—while it was still a minor disturbance/tropical depression.
- **Operational Impact:** The National Hurricane Center issued a Category 5 warning when the storm was still of very low intensity, giving local officials approximately a 3-day lead time to initiate evacuations and preparations. 
- **Historic Benchmark:** Peter Battaglia noted this was the lowest-intensity storm the National Hurricane Center had ever forecast to become a Category 5, with forecasters explicitly stating they were heavily informed by the AI model's 80% confidence scores. The storm ultimately produced record winds of 190 mph, resulting in 95 fatalities.

## Technological Shift: Traditional Numerical Models vs. AI Models
- **Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP):** Traditional forecasting relies on supercomputers running approximate fluid motion physics equations iteratively over coarse, blurry spatial grids. While a historic triumph of engineering, these models are computationally heavy and prone to compounding errors.
- **AI Statistical Learning:** DeepMind's approach fits a highly complex function to decades of historical weather records (such as ECMWF data spanning decades) to extrapolate future weather patterns based on past behavior.
- **Error Behavior:** Unlike traditional models that can "blow up" or diverge into implausible extremes when errors compound, AI statistical models tend to regress to the mean (predicting average weather when uncertain), yet remarkably retain the capacity to forecast extreme historical outliers like record-breaking hurricanes.

## Evolution of DeepMind's Weather Models
- **Phase 1 & 2 (Short-Term & Regional):** Early AI applications filled in fine-scale gaps for NWP models or predicted specific phenomena over short horizons (e.g., 90-minute rainfall models).
- **GraphCast (Global Deterministic):** One of the first Phase 3 models to simulate all weather over the entire Earth out to 10 days in a single representation, capturing large-scale structures (like entire hurricane widths) alongside local details.
- **GenCast (Probabilistic):** Introduced around 2023, shifting from a single deterministic guess to generating multiple plausible scenarios (probabilistic forecasting) using diffusion models and newly invented **Functional Generative Networks** (which inject statistical perturbations by slightly altering neural network weights).
- **WeatherNext 3 (End-to-End Integration):** 
  - **Raw Data Processing:** Moves beyond relying strictly on bureau estimates by ingesting raw satellite imagery and directly predicting high-quality weather station observations (e.g., airports) in an end-to-end architecture.
  - **Resolution & Frequency:** Operates at a higher spatial resolution with hourly forecasts (updated every hour due to hourly satellite changes) and native 6-hour window state predictions.
  - **New Variables:** Adds wind and solar variables designed to improve renewable energy supply forecasting and surface temperature/humidity metrics for electrical demand ("load") forecasting.

## Downstream Applications & Future Horizons
- **Renewable Energy & Load Forecasting:** Weather Next 3 supplies critical wind and solar variables for energy generation, while temperature and humidity metrics help power grids predict electrical demand peaks.
- **Agriculture:** Longer-term forecasting (weekly rainfall, monthly averages) aims to inform farmer decision-making regarding planting, harvesting, and deploying drought- or rain-resistant seeds.
- **Cross-Pollination with LLMs:** Future research will explore integrating text data (such as public discussions about weather) and allowing Large Language Models to interrogate weather models (e.g., asking conversational questions about specific mountain tops or valleys).

## Notable Quotes
> *"The better you do your sort of modeling and your machine learning and your evaluation and your data, you know, all the data handling, the better your models are going to be... same rules. just have to extract as much information about that data from the past as you can and then use it to forecast the future."*
> — Peter Battaglia

> *"We cannot know certain things. So it's important for our models to recognize that and to essentially be sort of humble in the sense of not trying to over... be overly confident about that."*
> — Peter Battaglia

> *"At the end of the day, I think if we want more accurate models, we need to be very diligent about keeping our focus on the evaluation and we just expand our evaluation beyond, you know, the temperature or the wind to again these many more variables and many more observations."*
> — Peter Battaglia

briefings.title: IFA Opening Keynote replay, presented by Jack Huynh

people.name: Jack Huynh
people.role: Senior Vice President and General Manager, AMD

briefings.tldr: AMD opened IFA 2026 by unveiling its "Era of Personal AI" vision, introducing high-performance local AI hardware—including Strix Halo, Gorgon Halo, and the Threadripper Halo Station—designed to run massive frontier-class models locally, maintain user privacy and context, and scale seamlessly from individual developer workstations to enterprise infrastructure.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AMD opened IFA 2026 by unveiling its "Era of Personal AI" vision, introducing high-performance local AI hardware—including Strix Halo, Gorgon Halo, and the Threadripper Halo Station—designed to run massive frontier-class models locally, maintain user privacy and context, and scale seamlessly from individual developer workstations to enterprise infrastructure.

## AMD Computing & AI Vision
* **Expanding Human Capability:** **Global impact of AMD technology:** Ranging from deep space exploration (Artemis II and Orion spacecraft) and precision medical robotics (Intuitive surgical systems) to climate research supercomputers (LUMI in Finland) and global entertainment infrastructure (EPYC, Threadripper, PlayStation 5 Pro).
* **The AI Paradigm Shift:** **Transition to agentic intelligence:** AI has progressed from reading and conversing to reasoning and acting via autonomous agents that can plan, use tools, and work in parallel.
* **The Token Consumption Crisis:** **Exploding enterprise compute demand:** 
  * **93% of companies** are currently exceeding their AI budgets.
  * **Monthly AI token processing** jumped from **0.7 quadrillion to 1.7 quadrillion** in just one year, with estimates reaching **120 quadrillion tokens per month by 2030**.
  * **Cloud cost disparity:** A single active user running agentic workflows can consume millions of tokens daily, translating to cloud costs near **€300 per day** (~€100,000 annually) for 15 million output tokens.

## Next-Generation AI PCs & Personal AI
* **The Three Pillars of Personal AI:** **Core design principles:** 
  * **Local compute:** Running powerful intelligence directly on personal hardware.
  * **Privacy and control:** Keeping sensitive data local and portable under user direction.
  * **Personal context:** Integrating a contextual layer so AI understands individual goals and workflows rather than just answering generic questions.
* **Strix Halo Hardware & Performance:** **Local frontier-class capability:** 
  * Features **120GB of unified memory**, enabling local execution of models up to **200 billion parameters**.
  * **Benchmark comparison:** The open-source model *Laguna S2.1* running locally on Strix Halo outperforms leading cloud models like *Cloud SANA 5* (which scores 70.3) on software engineering benchmarks without per-token cloud charges.
  * **Multitasking:** Capable of running **10 AI agents locally in parallel**.
* **Gorgon Halo & Gorgon Halo Box:** **Desktop and workstation power:** 
  * Boosts unified memory to **192 gigabytes**, supporting models with **200 to 300 billion parameters**.
  * *GLM 5.3 Flash* running locally on Gorgon Halo beats the cloud model *Cloud Fable 5* on benchmark tests.
  * Lenovo introduced the **ThinkCentre X** in Berlin powered by Gorgon Halo, designed to run 300 billion parameter models locally.
* **Project Sunday (Next-Gen HP ZBook):** **Mobile personal AI:** A new class of laptop featuring **190GB of unified memory** capable of generating real-time 3D worlds from a single prompt and playing demanding games like Flight Sim locally.

## Microsoft Partnership & Windows Integration
* **Pavan Davuluri (Microsoft) on Agentic Windows:** **OS-level transformation:** 
  * Windows is evolving from a tool to an active partner that can act across apps, services, and files via secure isolation boundaries (Microsoft Execution Containers).
  * **Hardware specs:** Acknowledged joint engineering on Gorgon Halo featuring **16 Zen 5 CPU cores**, an RDNA GPU, an efficient NPU, and **192GB of memory** running a **125 billion parameter model** locally.
* **Project Zenith:** **Developer-optimized experience:** 
  * A ready-to-code Windows experience coming pre-installed with VS Code, WSL, GitHub Copilot CLI, and PowerShell on hardware with a minimum of **64GB of UMA**.
  * Will be available out of the box on **AMD Ryzen AI Halo**.

## A New Class of AI System: Threadripper Halo Station
* **Threadripper Halo Station Architecture:** **Personal supercomputer workstation:** 
  * Designed for models with more than **one trillion parameters**.
  * Specs include **96 cores of Threadripper Pro**, **2 MI-350P Instinct accelerators** (with a path to four), up to **2 terabytes of system memory**, up to **576 gigabytes of HBM3E**, and full liquid cooling.

## Enterprise AI & Open Infrastructure
* **Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen (SUSE) on Scaling & Openness:** **Bridging local development to enterprise production:** 
  * **SUSE AI Factory and Rancher:** Provide a secure, supported path from local Ryzen AI Halo development workstations to enterprise-wide production scaling without discarding existing builds.
  * **Open Ecosystem:** Emphasized that developers and businesses need freedom of choice across models, frameworks, and infrastructure (local, private data center, edge, or cloud) without vendor lock-in, celebrating SUSE's **34th anniversary**.
  * **Unified Pool of Compute:** The long-term vision connects workstations, servers, data centers, and edge devices into a single open platform for AI.

## Notable Quotes
> *"Technology matters most when it puts more capability in people's hands. Today, I want to show you what happens when that capability becomes personal."*
> — **Jack Huynh**

> *"AI is evolving the Windows PC from a tool you use to a partner that can help us achieve more... Instead of just executing commands, the PC will understand workflows and just help people get done on what matters most to them."*
> — **Pavan Davuluri**

> *"The developer shouldn't have to think about each environment as a separate world. AMD brings compute across that entire spectrum. SUSE brings the open infrastructure and software to manage, connect and scale it."*
> — **Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen**

briefings.title: Inside the Race to Measure Frontier Intelligence
briefings.tldr: As public AI benchmarks saturate and self-reported model scores become increasingly unreliable, independent and continuously evolving evaluations are becoming critical for both enterprises measuring ROI and governments assessing safety risks.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
As public AI benchmarks saturate and self-reported model scores become increasingly unreliable, independent and continuously evolving evaluations are becoming critical for both enterprises measuring ROI and governments assessing safety risks.

## The Problem with Current AI Benchmarks
* **Saturation and Goodhart’s Law:** Public benchmarks are easily hacked and saturated as models optimize directly for the tests.
* **Flawed Self-Reporting:** Rayan Krishnan noted that when Meta released Llama 4, public open-source benchmarks showed incredible capabilities, but VALS's held-out private benchmarks revealed the model was actually underperforming.
* **The Need for Neutrality:** Rayan Krishnan explained that third-party evaluators must avoid conflicts of interest, drawing parallels to the Enron auditing scandal where mixing consulting with auditing corrupted incentives. VALS explicitly decided never to sell training data to labs to maintain independence.

## Enterprise ROI and the Shift to Token Spend
* **Escalating Costs:** Ben Horowitz noted the challenge of measuring fluid frontier intelligence compared to traditional Gartner quadrants. Rayan Krishnan shared an example from a Fortune 10 company where an engineer's budget increased from $100 to $300 per day, causing peak productivity to shift to 4:00 PM–6:00 PM when rate limits reset.
* **Token Spend vs. Salaries:** Rayan Krishnan recounted a VALS internal experiment where a token-maxing test resulted in spending $1.5 million in a month on free tokens—which was 10x higher than employee salaries for that month.
* **Val Smith Enterprise Product:** Rayan Krishnan introduced Val Smith, a tool allowing companies to take their GitHub codebase and build internal coding benchmarks to determine the most performant and Pareto-optimal models for their specific repositories.

## Pre-Release Infrastructure and Evolving Testing
* **The 6-Hour Pre-Release Window:** Rayan Krishnan described how VALS went from co-founders pulling all-nighters to running distributed evaluations at maximum rate limits using an internal system called "Steve, the economic VALS employee."
* **Handling Complex Workflows:** Rayan Krishnan noted that as evaluations become more complex (testing agentic work over hours, days, or weeks), sample sizes shrink while rubrics and criteria grow significantly larger (e.g., testing 50 full-stack web applications rather than millions of static images).
* **Always a Higher Peak:** Rayan Krishnan outlined VALS's unofficial motto and practice of deprecating saturated benchmarks and perpetually constructing new mountains for foundation model labs to summit.

## Specialized Indexes and Frontier Metrics
* **Economic Applications:** Rayan Krishnan highlighted VALS's finance agent benchmark (used by major financial institutions) and VI codebench for full-stack web application generation.
* **Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI):** Rayan Krishnan discussed the newly released RSI Index, which creates an apples-to-apples way to benchmark pre-training, post-training, and harness-level engineering proxies across frontier labs.

## Policy, Government Coordination, and Sovereign AI
* **Division of Labor:** Ben Horowitz compared the AI policy challenge to the MPAA rating system ("I know it when I see it"), arguing that governments are well-suited to set and enforce rules, while competent private companies must evaluate whether those rules are broken.
* **Information Sharing:** Rayan Krishnan stated that VALS regularly briefs executive and legislative branches on model capabilities and risks, helping policymakers ground abstract conversations in empirical data.
* **Global Verification:** Rayan Krishnan discussed the paradox of sovereign AI investments and suggested that international coordination on catastrophic risks (like cyber, bio, and RSI) will eventually require a shared language of evaluations, comparing it to Reagan's "trust but verify" doctrine for nuclear stockpiles.

## Notable Quotes
> "Every time a new trillion-dollar industry emerges, there's a need for this independent testing group."
> — Rayan Krishnan

> "It's a little bit reminiscent of the MPAA, right? Where it's like, what's art, what's porn, where's the line... and there's no—and the famous line is, well, I know it when I see it."
> — Ben Horowitz

> "As we talk about the existential concern for enterprises, I think it is this kind of direction we're shifting in where token spend may start to eclipse salary spend."
> — Rayan Krishnan

briefings.title: Tony Hawk inspiring us for 72 minutes straight
briefings.tldr: Skateboarding legend Tony Hawk shares how unrelenting obsession, grassroots philanthropy, and a refusal to quit propelled him from a misfit teen to a global icon.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Skateboarding legend Tony Hawk shares how unrelenting obsession, grassroots philanthropy, and a refusal to quit propelled him from a misfit teen to a global icon. He and the My First Million hosts also discuss the business of skateboarding, iconic video games, and aging gracefully in an extreme sport.

## Philanthropy & Skate Park Infrastructure
- **Tony Hawk Foundation:** 
  - **Founding Context:** Started in **2002** with his brother and sister to support kids in underserved areas who lacked safe, legal places to skate. 
  - **Scope:** Has contributed to close to **1,000 skate parks** to date.
  - **Early Grants:** Initial grants ranged from **$5,000 to $10,000**, which provided crucial municipal validation and pushed stalled local approval processes over the finish line.
  - **Endorsement Funding:** Hawk mandated that **10% to 20%** of his personal corporate endorsement contracts went straight to the foundation.
- **Charity: Water Parallel:** Shaan Puri highlights Charity: Water's business model (GPS tracking, flow meters, and donor trips) as a masterclass in giving donors concrete, transparent proof of impact—similar to Hawk's philosophy of building physical, lasting concrete skate parks.

## The Price of Greatness & The 900
- **Obsession over Accolades:** Hawk notes his childhood was defined by a relentless, singular focus on learning new tricks rather than chasing contest wins or magazine covers.
- **Financial Reality Check:** During his early professional career, Hawk had **$640 in the bank** and bought a Honda scooter to get to the skate park independently.
- **The 1991 Slump:** Following a popularity boom driven by *Back to the Future* (1985), Hawk's income dropped by **half every month** in 1991; his Airwalk shoe sponsor cut his monthly payments from **$1,500 to $1,000, then $500, and eventually $300** within a single year, forcing him to pay mortgages by doing odd jobs and Hollywood stunt consulting.
- **The 900 Landmark (1999):** 
  - Landed the historic 900 on live ESPN during a best-trick event after **20 minutes** of attempts.
  - Had **never landed the trick** in practice prior to that moment; previous attempts resulted in severe injuries, including a broken rib in **1994** at around **2:00 PM** on a weekday in a warehouse.

## Video Game Empire: Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater (THPS)
- **Early Rejections:** Pitched a skateboarding game engine around **1997** to companies like Nintendo, where one executive dismissed it by stating, *"Skateboarding isn't even popular. Why would a skateboarding video game be popular?"*
- **Activision Partnership:** Connected with Activision (who had recently released *Apocalypse* starring Bruce Willis, where early test builds literally featured Bruce Willis on a skateboard doing ollies).
- **The Buyout Offer:** Right before the game's release, Activision offered Hawk a **$500,000 buyout** to surrender future royalties, which he declined to "let it ride."
- **Explosive Success:** 
  - By the release of the fourth game, **four out of the top 10 best-selling video games** were *Tony Hawk's Pro Skater* titles.
  - Culminated in a single royalty payout meeting where an Activision executive slid a check across the table for **$4.5 million**.

## Current Business Ventures & Investments
- **Birdhouse Skateboards:** Founded in **1992** with partner Perry Wheeler; survived bleak early years, hit peak profitability and cultural mainstreaming between **1999 and 2005**, and maintains its classic **$60 deck price point** despite low profit margins.
- **900 Films:** Video production company handling media projects, commercials, and work with brands like Liquid Death.
- **Restaurants:** Invested in failed concepts like Counter Burger in San Diego, but currently operates **Chicken Hawk**, a Nashville hot chicken restaurant in Encinitas featuring 90s skate culture vibes.
- **Angel Investments:** Invested alongside Silicon Valley figures in notable companies including **Nest**, **Blue Bottle**, **DocuSign**, and **Events.com** (nearing an IPO).

## Aging, Culture, and Skateboarding Longevity
- **Skate Culture & Media:** Recalls making DIY zines in **1982** (selling them for **$50 cents** at Del Mar Skate Ranch) before the era of skate magazines like *Thrasher* and *Transworld*.
- **Aging and Stretching:** Hawk shares specific pre-skate warm-up routines (such as deep kneeling and joint rotations) to combat the physical toll of skating approaching age **58**.
- **Skate Park Etiquette:** Identifies prime skate park hours for older skaters as **8:00 AM to 11:00 AM**, avoiding peak crowds and high-impact street skating runs that risk police intervention (such as a **$150 ticket** he received in Oceanside in **1990** for skating the boardwalk).

## Notable Quotes
> "I never considered quitting skating cuz I never started skating for money. So even if I had to find a quote real job at the time, I was going to find time to skate."
> — Tony Hawk

> "That was the sort of state of things in 1994... I broke my rib on a ramp in a warehouse at around 2 p.m. on a weekday and I had to go pick up my oldest son... barely able to breathe cuz I had broken my rib."
> — Tony Hawk

> "At that time in my life, someone saying a half a million dollars sounded like a half a gazillion dollars. Like I had never heard anyone speak those words unless they're talking about some fantastical person that we will never meet."
> — Tony Hawk

briefings.title: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Fireside Chat at SMU Cox School of Business
briefings.tldr: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joined SMU President Jay Hartzell and moderator Ray Washburne for a fireside chat discussing economic policy, global market dynamics, artificial intelligence, and his journey from global finance to public service.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent joined SMU President Jay Hartzell and moderator Ray Washburne for a fireside chat discussing economic policy, global market dynamics, artificial intelligence, and his journey from global finance to public service.

## Background & Personal History
* **Early Hardships:** **Scott Bessent** grew up in South Carolina where his father, a successful real estate developer, suffered severe financial setbacks due to over-leverage and poor decisions, forcing Bessent to work as a busboy at age 9.
* **Risk Management & Perspective:** This early experience deeply ingrained in Bessent a respect for risk management, avoiding over-leverage, and maintaining long-term perspective across economic cycles (such as the Texas oil bust, Asian financial crisis, and dot-com bust).
* **Education & Influences:** Bessent attended Yale University, studying history, philosophy, and psychology rather than traditional economics, describing himself as an "economic historian" rather than an economist.

## Economic Policy, Debt, and Growth
* **Spending vs. Revenue:** **Scott Bessent** stated that the U.S. does not have a revenue problem but a spending problem, aiming to contain spending and achieve 3% GDP growth to grow out of national debt.
* **Economic Stimulus & Tax Policy:** Cited the "Working Families Tax Cut" (one big beautiful bill) featuring full expensing for equipment, factories, and farm structures alongside working-class tax relief (no tax on tips or overtime, and social security tax exemptions for 85% of seniors).
* **Foreign Policy & Currency Interventions:** **Scott Bessent** explained using the U.S. balance sheet and Exchange Stabilization Fund for foreign policy goals (such as bridging Argentina during elections) to foster pro-market Western Hemisphere allies and counter opposition panics.
* **Energy Markets:** Discussed the tight correlation between interest rates and energy prices, predicting future oil over-supply driven by U.S., Venezuelan, and eventual Middle Eastern/Ukrainian normalization.

## Global Competitiveness & Artificial Intelligence
* **Competing Economic Ideologies:** **Scott Bessent** contrasted the U.S. growth agenda with European economic sclerosis and the Chinese state-planning model, predicting the U.S. model will prevail.
* **AI Ecosystem & Compute Power:** Highlighted America's organic AI boom, noting the U.S. will hold 80% of global computing power by 2028 (compared to China's projected 15%), while criticizing European risk-aversion and heavy regulation.
* **Impact on Jobs and Small Business:** Advised students that AI will not replace them, but someone who knows how to use AI will; noted a record surge in small business formations enabled by AI tools.

## Financial Literacy & Local Impact
* **Trump Accounts:** **Scott Bessent** highlighted Treasury's financial literacy initiatives and "Trump Accounts," seeded with $1,000 for children born during the term, augmented by a $6.25 billion donation from Susan and Michael Dell ($250 per child outside top 20 zip codes).
* **Texas Economy:** **Ray Washburne** and **Scott Bessent** praised Texas and Dallas ("Y'all Street") as high-pressure, pro-growth labs for the Trump economy, drawing massive domestic migration away from over-regulated states like California and New York.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Global Computing Dominance:** The U.S. will control 80% of global computing power by 2028, up from 50% in 2025, while China will hold approximately 15% — Scott Bessent
* **Anthropic Valuation:** Anthropic will likely go public at a $2 trillion valuation — Scott Bessent
* **AI Small Business Boom:** AI will continue driving a record-setting wave of new small business formations, enabling companies that previously required 12 to 20 people to be run by just 1 to 3 people — Scott Bessent (referencing Marc Andreessen)

## Notable Quotes
> "If I believe this stuff, I'd be as upset as these folks are. I would put my passport in my mouth and swim to Portugal if I believed everything they were saying."
> — **Scott Bessent**

> "We don't have a revenue problem, we have a spending problem."
> — **Scott Bessent**

> "AI is probably not going to take your job. Someone who knows how to use AI will take your job."
> — **Scott Bessent**
